posts.author: BonestockNA
posts.content:
That's a surge and it could be caused by quite a few things.  Bad fuel injector(s), poor combustion in one or more cylinders, idle speed control (IAC motor hunting), air leak somewhere or something putting intermittent load on the engine like an accessory drive or trans/torque converter issue (saw the ect pwr light on the dash so I assume AT).  I'm leaning towards air leak, leaky cold start injector or combustion problem somewhere the way it sounds.  You could try to disconnect and plug the fuel supply to the cold start injector and see if your idle smooths out.  







Also if the temperatures are cold when you start this engine it does have a highcam feature that will raise the rpm and slowly bring it down as water temperature rises.

posts.author: BonestockNA
posts.content:
1. You should definitely have a replacement gasket ready for the IAC motor.  



2. I don't think your TB replacement gasket is an issue as long as it fits correctly.  







I make some of these types of gaskets sometimes with good results.  







The reason by the way that I mentioned the cold start injector could be the reason for the idle surge is this was something I remember seeing on some of these vehicles back in the day.  When the fuel rail is charged and the cold start injector is not sealing 100%, the pressure pulsing in the rail can cause the injector to weep into the plenum and cause the idle surging.  The engine runs fine otherwise. 



The problem was fixed by replacing the cold start injector valve.

posts.author: 3p141592654
posts.content:
You must first confirm the IDL switch in the throttle position sensor is set correctly. Easy to do.






Turn off AC, lights and put trans in Neutral if A/T


Jump the ECU to diag mode using paper clip TE1 to E1


Turn on ignition


To verify the IDL signal is working correctly, observe if the 
check engine light flashes
 at a steady, 0.26 second interval (indicating no codes, and thus, the IDL signal is correctly received as "closed").


If the light flashes code 51  the IDL signal is not being received correctly.


Stepping on the gas should open the IDL signal and cause a code 51.  Turning on the lights, AC, or putting the A/T in gear will also set code 51 so beware of that.







If the IDL switch is not set right you can calibrate it per the TSRM.  Its a simple job.  But your idle will never be correct if the IDL switch is not working right because the IDL switch actuates the idle software and changes the way timing is managed.

posts.author: BonestockNA
posts.content:
I wanted to address your question about the EFI connectors.  The connector you are showing is broken and the insulation on the wires looks like its flaking off.  You can buy those connectors.  Look for  pinned connectors with pig tails on them.  You can work back up the harness a few inches until you get back to sound wiring and then solder the new connector leads in.  Use heat shrink to seal the joints.  Wire colors are not so important.  Just note the orientation of the connectors and which wire colors are on the left & right pins (ie which side is ground and which side is your channel output).  The new connector will need to match the same orientation when you hook up to the old wiring.  







The fuel injection system is a semi-sequential system.  There are only 3 channels so each channel will service 2 cylinders at the same time in a batch firing scheme.

posts.author: 3p141592654
posts.content: There is no idle stop screw.  The dashpot adjustment should not affect idle.  Remove the throttle rod from the throttle body and check if the throttle consistently. snaps back to closed position when you open it by hand. If the TB is sluggish or inconsistent figure out what is hanging it up.  If the TB is okay, then its your cable assembly.  Could be the bellcrank on top of the engine (plastic bushing disintegrate over time), or the cable is rusty, or the gas pedal is rusty.  You should check all those places for issues.

posts.author: BonestockNA
posts.content:
Good job finding the air leak.  That's usually the cause of performance issues when every thing else seems all good.  







The cause of this is a real PINTA.  If the threads were already repaired it probably was not done correctly.  A good helecoil repair usually holds.  You are supposed to put the thread coil in with red lock tight.   If the coil will thread back in OK maybe the solution is to lock tight it, let it set, then install the bolt.  







If everything is stripped out then you might need to step up the bolt size and re-drill and thread the hole for the new size.  I don't remember what those were... M8 sounds about right?  Step up to M10 if you have the room.  Another option may be to use a thru bolt if you can get a nut on the other side.  You just need to clamp the piece together.  If you want to start over you should be able to find those intakes around used.
